CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
46-year-old female presents for follow-up. Reports significant improvement in anxiety symptoms since starting Buspar, recently prescribed by Dr. Brown. Experienced severe anxiety in November and December of last year, predominantly during work hours. Initially noted premenstrual pattern with peaks one week prior to menses, which evolved into unpredictable episodes without clear temporal relationship. Patient was started on Singulair by Dr. Ward during that time; was counseled that this medication can potentially cause anxiety. Unclear if this was contributory to her symptoms. Currently taking progesterone for menstrual regulation. Discussed possible hormonal component and identified significant work-related stressors, particularly her role in COVID-19 pandemic response including establishing evaluation centers and COVID clinics, and managing patient result delivery processes. Patient acknowledged experiencing guilt regarding her anxiety given that she was not working in intensive care setting. Recently discontinued Camila birth control after experiencing significant appetite increase while on the medication; appetite has normalized since stopping. Denies weight gain but reports weight loss over the past 6 months. Currently feeling significantly improved.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies major systemic complaints. Left breast tenderness noted, particularly in lower aspect. Reports palpable breast lumps which she states are smaller than previously but still present. History of breast tenderness and clogging with prior breastfeeding. Mild vaginal itching and discomfort managed with topical cream applied once weekly with good symptom control. Patient needs refill of this medication.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Abnormal Pap smear approximately 2009, required frequent surveillance until normalization. Pap smear in 2019 with negative/negative results. Benign breast cysts/lumps.

MEDICATIONS
Buspar
Progesterone
Topical vaginal cream (applied once weekly)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at approximately age 45.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works in healthcare, directly involved in COVID-19 pandemic response. Vaccinated against COVID-19. Son vaccinated (first dose completed). Husband and daughter unvaccinated citing concerns about long-term effects.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert and well-appearing
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal breathing
Neck: Palpation reveals small bumps; patient notes these are smaller than previously
Breasts: Left breast slightly denser with tenderness elicited particularly in the lower aspect on palpation. Bilateral palpable lumps noted, smaller than previously noted but still present. Right breast without specific findings.
Genitourinary: External genitalia and vaginal area appear grossly normal without acute findings

RESULTS
No laboratory or imaging studies obtained this visit.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety disorder: Significantly improved on Buspar with good tolerability. Etiology appears multifactorial including possible hormonal factors, work-related stress, and pandemic-related stressors. Continue current regimen.

2. Breast lumps/cysts: Examination findings consistent with benign breast disease. Continue monitoring given patient concern and significant family history (mother with breast cancer diagnosed at age 45). Will send referral to breast surgery specialist for in-office ultrasound as extension of physical examination, expert evaluation, and expedited intervention if needed. Specialist office will contact patient within a couple of business days to schedule appointment.

3. Cervical cancer screening: Last Pap was 2019 (negative/negative). Prior abnormal Pap in 2009. Repeat Pap recommended given time elapsed since last screening, history of abnormality, and potential increased risk from pandemic-related stress and immunocompromise. Patient agreeable.

4. Vaginal discomfort: Continue current topical cream regimen (once weekly application). Prescription will be refilled.

5. Follow-up: As needed, or per recommendations from breast specialist.
